title.en: Securing Language Model and Agent Applications

tagline: Attack a working agent over repeated trials, then contain it so that a fooled model breaks nothing important
description: Participants attack and then defend a working agent: a synthetic clearance assistant for a fictional port authority that reads importers' emails and invoices, searches a tariff knowledge base, remembers each importer, runs code to compute duties and acts through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. They threat-model it, run injection, exfiltration and poisoning attacks over repeated trials, then contain it with a sandbox and egress rules, scoped short-lived delegated tokens, separated privileged and quarantined model calls, measured guardrails and approvals placed where a person adds safety. Red-team programmes are AE-407.
audience: Practitioners. Engineers who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: a deployed model or language model application they built and can explain.
prerequisites: AE-207 Responsible and Secure AI Engineering Practice
AE-302 Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses
Has built a tool-calling agent and read its traces
Runs containers locally and changes their network settings
Setup: a laptop processor with uv, or Google Colab. Nothing downloads a model and no key is needed; a free hosted model is optional. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1 and read labs/PREWORK.md.

outcomes.text: Prepare a threat model with data flows, trust boundaries and threats mapped to recognised risk lists and adversary-technique catalogues, given the clearance agent, its tool list and the classification of its data
outcomes.evidence: a threat model with at least 12 threats, each mapped and scored on the national four-by-four likelihood and impact scale

outcomes.text: Test the application with direct, indirect, memory and tool-poisoning attacks in Arabic and English over repeated trials, given a starter attack corpus and a fixed budget of model calls
outcomes.evidence: an attack log with a success rate and interval for each technique

outcomes.text: Design containment for generated code and outbound actions with a sandbox, an egress allowlist and recipient rules, given the attack log and 50 benign tasks
outcomes.evidence: a rerun in which every logged exfiltration path fails while at least 95% of benign tasks still pass

outcomes.text: Build delegated authorisation in which each tool call carries an exchanged token with one audience, a narrow scope and a short lifetime, given two protocol servers that share one API key and a containerised identity provider
outcomes.evidence: a token audit and a confused-deputy test that fails against the hardened design

outcomes.text: Configure input guardrails and output validation and measure their false-positive and false-negative rates, given bilingual attack and benign sets
outcomes.evidence: a tuning report with the chosen thresholds and both error rates

outcomes.text: Defend a residual-risk statement after another team attacks the hardened agent, with each confirmed finding turned into a regression test, given a timed red-team exercise
outcomes.evidence: a findings report keyed to risk-list entries, a passing regression suite and a live defence

case_study.name: Fanar Ports Authority
case_study.summary: Fanar Ports Authority is a fictional Gulf-coast port authority. Its platform team built Mukhallis, a clearance assistant that reads importers' emails and invoices, searches the tariff notes, remembers each importer, runs code to compute duties and acts through two protocol servers, the case system and outbound communications. Participants take it as found, threat-model it, attack it over repeated trials and contain it. Every one of the 400 importer records, the 200 emails and invoices, the tariff notes and the attack texts is synthetic, generated with a fixed seed, and planted with the weaknesses the labs find: one API key shared by both servers, a server that acts for anyone, a link inside the duty tool's work folder, a tool description that changes after approval, and legitimate Arabic requests that a guardrail blocks.

format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Capstone: red-team day and live defence
days.subtitle: Attack another team's hardened agent, harden your own, defend the residual risk

capstone.summary: Red-team day: a timed attack on another team's hardened agent, then a final hardening pass on one's own, submitted as a public repository with threat model, attack log, findings and regression suite and defended live; the follow-up task re-runs the suite after a scripted model change
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository per team holding the threat model (at least 12 threats, mapped and scored), the attack log with a success rate and interval per technique, the findings report keyed to risk-list entries, the hardened build and the regression suite passing in continuous integration, with the prompts of any attacker model logged and the commit history kept. Then a ten-minute live defence of the residual-risk statement and five minutes of questions: the team reproduces one attack on the build as found and shows why it now fails.
